newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB quarterly report sees no inflation danger.
newsitem.headline: SNB quarterly report sees no inflation danger.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank in its quarterly report for March said there appeared to be no inflation danger at the moment in the economy.

In a report completed on February 13 and updated in the interim for presentation at a meeting of the SNB's board on March 7, the SNB noted that several factors continued to show that inflation, and inflationary fears, remained in check.
It also noted that "recessive tendencies" in the Swiss economy continued in the fourth quarter of 1996, and in the first quarter of 1997 there was no real sign of an economic turnaround.

"Long-term interest rates currently give no indication of an increase in inflationary expectations. Banks' domestic loan activity offers no stimulus. The large degree of unutilised capacity in wide areas of the economy allow one to surmise that the expected economic recovery would not unleash any significant rise in inflation," the SNB said.
